content.value_statement: Keeping current with research requires repeated searching, filtering, reading, and organizing. This skill defines a configurable workflow for recurring discovery, delivery, and archival.
actual_capabilities: Defines recurring searches across arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref, and optionally Semantic Scholar.
Deduplicates candidate papers using DOI, arXiv ID, OpenAlex ID, and normalized titles.
Ranks papers with a configurable six-dimension, 100-point scoring rubric.
Creates concise digests with reading depth, methods, key results, limitations, and stable links.
Provides templates for scheduled delivery, raw-note archival, gap analysis, and review compilation.
limitations: Scheduling and delivery require a compatible local scheduler and configured messaging integration.
Search quality depends on source availability, API limits, keywords, and accessible metadata.
Full-text analysis is unavailable for inaccessible or paywalled papers.
Scores prioritize candidates but do not replace expert review or citation verification.

use_cases.title: Monitor a Research Topic
use_cases.description: Create a daily or weekly digest of new papers for a defined topic, keyword set, and exclusion list.

use_cases.title: Build a Team Reading Queue
use_cases.description: Rank recent candidates and deliver focused summaries that help a research group select papers for deeper reading.

use_cases.title: Map a Literature Gap
use_cases.description: Search related systems, classify direct and adjacent evidence, and prepare a reproducible gap report for a new project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Weekly Digest
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a weekly literature pipeline for [topic]. Search [sources], review the last [days] days, and return the top [count] papers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one research topic

prompt_templates.title: Configure Scoring and Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Monitor [topic] using these keywords: [keywords]. Exclude [terms]. Score [candidate count] papers and deliver the top [final count] to [target].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Verified Archive Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a recurring pipeline for [topic]. Deduplicate by stable identifiers, label reading depth, archive raw notes under [path], and verify delivery separately.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Research Gap Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate whether [research question] is a documented gap. Search exact and adjacent terms across three sources. Record queries, evidence tiers, limitations, and next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced evidence mapping and review planning

output_examples.input: Track machine learning methods for marine concrete durability during the last seven days.
output_examples.output: A ranked digest lists five deduplicated papers with scores, reading depth, methods, specific results, limitations, and stable source links.

output_examples.input: Check whether a four-component material system has been studied and document the search.
output: A concise conclusion distinguishes a confirmed gap from partial overlap.
A subsystem table classifies direct, adjacent, and unrelated evidence.
A reproducibility section records search terms, sources, hit counts, and follow-up work.

output_examples.input: Prepare a reusable daily literature push for a research group.
output_examples.output: A configurable profile defines topics, exclusions, source priority, scoring weights, delivery target, archive settings, and a verification checklist.

best_practices: Review keywords and score distributions after several runs, then adjust weights with the user.
Label every paper as full text, abstract only, metadata only, or project page reviewed.
Verify scheduling, delivery, archival, deduplication, and failure alerts as separate stages.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a high score as proof of paper quality or relevance.
Do not claim full-text findings when only metadata or an abstract was available.
Do not place private chat identifiers, API keys, or machine-specific paths in shared templates.

faq.question: Which literature sources does this skill support?
faq.answer: It describes searches across arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref, and optionally Semantic Scholar, with graceful degradation when a source is unavailable.

faq.question: Does the skill create scheduled jobs by itself?
faq.answer: It provides scheduling prompts and verification guidance. Actual scheduling requires a compatible local scheduler and user configuration.

faq.question: Can it send digests to messaging platforms?
faq.answer: Yes, when the agent has a configured messaging integration and an authorized destination such as Feishu or Telegram.

faq.question: How does it prevent duplicate papers?
faq.answer: It compares DOI, arXiv ID, OpenAlex ID, and normalized titles before selecting and archiving papers.

faq.question: What happens when full text is unavailable?
faq.answer: The workflow uses available abstracts or metadata and labels the reading depth so users can judge evidence quality.

faq.question: Does the scoring system replace expert judgment?
faq.answer: No. The rubric prioritizes candidates, while researchers must verify relevance, methods, results, and citations.
